pr_body:
This change introduces a new arbitrary index version so that it is not possible to restore 8.12 index in 8.11.

Fixes: #100291
pr_comments: In addition to my [comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/101906#discussion_r1400893194) on the future of the underlying version check, after discussion with Henning I think we can still merge this PR. It won't make the situation any worse (we need to handle moving the metadata back to storing semantic version, and account for many potential index versions). Additional index versions won't hurt that work, and it would be good to get this test running again.
In context of the above comment, could somebody please review again and approve?

comments: I've muted this one as well.
This is indeed broken by the 8.12 version commit 132220bf83b1b8177a7c83906abf9bbbb830c8bd, but the cause is not clear. CCR failure, so Distributed will have a better idea what the issue is here

This test verifies that and older cluster can not follow and index created in a newer cluster.
Previously this check was linked to elasticsearch version, now it is updated to use `IndexVersion` instead: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8e6e0e59ea34be29a6495f0680944d6a7f559756/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/snapshots/RestoreService.java#L973-L982

Above check is failing as the latest `IndexVersion` is the same (`8_500_003`) for both versions:
* 8.11: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/57a067c08a37739ccf360ad4ec19063aca920ee0/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/IndexVersion.java#L128
* current main: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8a1db8c6c3ffa8028b98c9c1393aee9d9ea4d6f5/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/IndexVersions.java#L89
and this currently allows an older 8.11 version to follow an index with the same version from the never main version.

If this is expected then _some_ elasticsearch versions become forward compatible re CCR.
If this is not expected then we need to introduce a new IndexVersion for every minor elasticsearch release.

If there hasn't actually been any change to the index format, would we expect anything to go wrong if the "new" cluster followed the "old" cluster? In other words, would we be bumping the version in order to avoid bugs, or would we be bumping it so that it's easy to describe CCR compatibility between clusters?
This kept failing (twice today) so I backported the mute to 8.11

review_comments: For my understanding, how does this new IndexVersion get used, since I do not see it anywhere used in this PR?

It means that `org.elasticsearch.index.IndexVersion#current` is strictly greater in `main` than in `8.11` which allows us to enforce the right version barrier between `8.11.1-SNAPSHOT` and `8.12.0-SNAPSHOT` builds. Otherwise they have the same `org.elasticsearch.index.IndexVersion#current` which makes ES think that their indices are compatible, which breaks some test assumptions.
@kingherc, `def` adds this version into `IndexVersions#IDS`. It is used later via `LATEST_DEFINED = VERSION_IDS.lastEntry().getValue();`

nit: can the name be more tailored to what this is guarding? As it is, others might think a new "ES_VERSION_XXX" is needed for ever minor, yet this is specifically a guard for a bug around snapshots metadata in 8.11 right?
There is nothing preventing such thing from happening during the next release. I would add it every time we release for simplicity.

++ I think this needs a discussion about how to handle it long-term, whether we want to preserve this behaviour (and today's tests) or not. If we want to do this every time, we need to update the release/version-bump process.
I thought this was a different issue. I've added this topic for discussion to the core/infra agenda.

After discussing with core/infra, I think the test issue can be assigned over to core/infra for resolution. We don't want to add new IndexVersions here, but rather slightly relax our "nothing can have semantic version checks" rule. We will follow up with a couple changes:
* Make the snapshot metadata check only occur for on-prem, and go back to semantic versions
* Add facilities for semantic version checks that will only run in serverless. This would be for things that serverless doesn't need to care about (like this too-new-index check).
